result.title: DAYJOB: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Professional Work
result.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. An earlier version was accepted to the 2nd Workshop on Agentic AI Benchmarks and Applications for Enterprise Tasks (AABA4ET) at NeurIPS 2026. Evaluation harness: https://github.com/surge-ai/dayjob
result.summary: Professional work often starts with a brief request that leaves the professional to work out what is needed, which documents matter, and whether the request's premise holds. We introduce DAYJOB, a benchmark of 130 tasks built by professionals in healthcare (50) and finance (80). The tasks are estimated to take a professional 13.6 hours on average in healthcare and 16.6 in finance. Each task is a containerized Harbor environment with an expert rubric of binary criteria (median 47.5 and 57.5 per task) that an agentic judge applies to the delivered files, and an attempt passes only if it meets every criterion. Across 30 model configurations from 13 developers, the strongest, Claude Opus 5.5, passes 24.7% of healthcare and 23.9% of finance attempts, and the median configuration passes 0.6% and 2.5%. In case studies, agents accept premises that the record contradicts and carry wrong inputs through otherwise consistent analyses. We release all healthcare tasks, 50 of the 80 finance tasks, the evaluation harness, and the leaderboard.

AI.brief_summary: DAYJOB 是一个面向长周期专业工作（医疗、金融）的 130 任务基准，任务需专业人员平均 13–16 小时完成，采用容器化环境与二元专家评分标准，只有全部标准满足才算通过，并报告了 13 家开发者 30 种模型配置的通过率。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及 latent 视觉推理，但案例显示智能体会接受与记录相矛盾的前提、并把错误输入贯穿后续分析，这与 LVR 关注的证据筛选、前提核验、何时获取外部证据与停止决策可能相关，可供核查其任务分解与失败模式是否能迁移为多模态推理的诊断设计。
